title_en: Beautiful Places in China (12/20): The Gardens of Suzhou, a Scene at Every Step
note_en: The particle 着 after a verb describes a state that simply exists, which is how Chinese paints a scene: 池边堆叠着形态各异的太湖石 "piled up along the edge of the pond are Taihu rocks of every shape." Notice that the place comes first and the thing comes last, like English "There are..." or "Along the pond lie..."; 曲折的回廊连接着各个亭台 works the same way. 了 would report a completed action instead of a lasting state.
